claims.evidence: This is stated with reference to Kang et al., 2008.

claims.claim: FKBPs act as chaperones to prevent protein aggregation under stress conditions.
claims.source: Independent of their PPIase activity, FKBPs act as chaperones to prevent protein aggregation under stress conditions (Bose et al., 1996; Furutani et al., 2000).
claims.evidence: This is stated with references to Bose et al., 1996 and Furutani et al., 2000.

claims.claim: Some FKBP variants play a role in cellular signaling or gene regulation.
claims.source: Furthermore, some FKBP variants play a role in cellular signaling or gene regulation (Yang et al., 2001; Kasahara et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is stated with references to Yang et al., 2001 and Kasahara et al., 2020.

claims.claim: Human FKBP12 forms a complex with FK506 and rapamycin.
claims.source: Human FKBP12, for instance, is best known for its ability to form a complex with the immunosuppressant drugs FK506 and rapamycin.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a well-known property of HsFKBP12.

claims.claim: The FKBP12-FK506 complex inhibits the phosphatase activity of calcineurin.
claims.source: These complexes inhibit the phosphatase activity of calcineurin and the kinase activity of mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR), respectively (Cardenas et al., 1995).
claims.evidence: This is stated with reference to Cardenas et al., 1995.

claims.claim: The FKBP12-rapamycin complex inhibits the kinase activity of mTOR.
claims.source: These complexes inhibit the phosphatase activity of calcineurin and the kinase activity of mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR), respectively (Cardenas et al., 1995).
claims.evidence: This is stated with reference to Cardenas et al., 1995.

claims.claim: Inhibition of calcineurin and mTOR by FKBP12 complexes results in decreased T-cell activation.
claims.source: Amongst many other effects, this inhibition results in decreased T-cell activation.
claims.evidence: This is stated as one of the effects of calcineurin and mTOR inhibition.

claims.claim: HsFKBP12 does not interact with mTOR or calcineurin in the absence of drugs.
claims.source: Of note, the regulatory role of HsFKBP12 depends on the presence of rapamycin or FK506. In the absence of drugs, this immunophilin neither interacts with mTOR nor with calcineurin and does hence not affect activity of these key components of eukaryotic cells.
claims.evidence: This is stated to emphasize the drug-dependent nature of HsFKBP12's regulatory role.

claims.claim: PfFKBP35 harbors PPIase and chaperoning activity in vitro.
claims.source: Similar to its homologs in model organisms, PfFKBP35 harbors PPIase and chaperoning activity in vitro (Monaghan and Bell, 2005).
claims.evidence: This is stated with reference to Monaghan and Bell, 2005.

claims.claim: The role of PfFKBP35 in P. falciparum remains elusive.
claims.source: Despite sharing key features with FKBPs of other eukaryotes, its role in P. falciparum remains elusive.
claims.evidence: This is stated to highlight the gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claims.claim: PfFKBP35 is believed to interact with heat shock proteins (HSPs).
claims.source: PfFKBP35 is believed to interact with heat shock proteins (HSPs) and co-immunoprecipitates with cytoskeletal factors of P. falciparum (Leneghan and Bell, 2015).
claims.evidence: This is stated with reference to Leneghan and Bell, 2015.

claims.claim: PfFKBP35 co-immunoprecipitates with cytoskeletal factors of P. falciparum.
claims.source: PfFKBP35 is believed to interact with heat shock proteins (HSPs) and co-immunoprecipitates with cytoskeletal factors of P. falciparum (Leneghan and Bell, 2015).
claims.evidence: This is stated with reference to Leneghan and Bell, 2015.

claims.claim: PfFKBP35 inhibits the phosphatase activity of recombinant calcineurin in an FK506-independent manner.
claims.source: While PfFKBP35 inhibits the phosphatase activity of recombinant calcineurin in an FK506-independent manner (Yoon et al., 2007; Kumar et al., 2005; Alag et al., 2009), it does not co-localize with calcineurin in vivo (Kumar et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: This is stated with references to Yoon et al., 2007; Kumar et al., 2005; and Alag et al., 2009.

claims.claim: PfFKBP35 does not co-localize with calcineurin in vivo.
claims.source: While PfFKBP35 inhibits the phosphatase activity of recombinant calcineurin in an FK506-independent manner (Yoon et al., 2007; Kumar et al., 2005; Alag et al., 2009), it does not co-localize with calcineurin in vivo (Kumar et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: This is stated with reference to Kumar et al., 2005.

claims.claim: PfFKBP35 is expressed throughout the 48 hr intra-erythrocytic development of P. falciparum.
claims.source: The protein is expressed throughout the 48 hr intra-erythrocytic development of P. falciparum and is found within the cytosol of ring stage parasites.
claims.evidence: This is stated based on previous observations.

claims.claim: PfFKBP35 is found within the cytosol of ring stage parasites.
claims.source: The protein is expressed throughout the 48 hr intra-erythrocytic development of P. falciparum and is found within the cytosol of ring stage parasites.
claims.evidence: This is stated based on previous observations.

claims.claim: In trophozoite and schizont stages, PfFKBP35 localizes to the nucleus.
claims.source: In the older trophozoite and the replicating schizont stages, the protein was reported to also localize to the nucleus (Kumar et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: This is stated with reference to Kumar et al., 2005.

claims.claim: A transposon-based mutagenesis screen suggests that PfFKBP35 is essential for intra-erythrocytic replication.
claims.source: While a transposon-based mutagenesis screen suggests that PfFKBP35 is essential for intra-erythrocytic replication (Zhang et al., 2018), neither its cellular function nor its essentiality was confirmed experimentally in live parasites.
claims.evidence: This is stated with reference to Zhang et al., 2018.

claims.claim: P. vivax and P. knowlesi encode FKBP homologs that exhibit comparable PPIase activities to PfFKBP35.
claims.source: The unknown role in parasite biology notwithstanding, PfFKBP35 is considered to be a viable drug target and, given the fact that P. vivax and P. knowlesi encode FKBP homologs that exhibit comparable PPIase activities (Alag et al., 2010; Goh et al., 2018), future FKBP-targeted therapies may be effective across different Plasmodium species.
claims.evidence: This is stated with references to Alag et al., 2010 and Goh et al., 2018.

claims.claim: Crystal structures of PfFKBP35 in complex with FK506 and rapamycin revealed high-affinity interactions with the FK506-binding domain.
claims.source: Crystal structures of PfFKBP35 in complex with FK506 and rapamycin revealed high-affinity interactions with the FK506-binding domain of the protein (Yoon et al., 2007; Bianchin et al., 2015; Kotaka et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This is stated with references to Yoon et al., 2007; Bianchin et al., 2015; and Kotaka et al., 2008.

claims.claim: FK506 inhibits the PPIase activity of recombinant PfFKBP35 in a dose-dependent manner.
claims.source: Consistent with these observations, in vitro enzyme activity assays showed that FK506 inhibits the PPIase activity of recombinant PfFKBP35 in a dose-dependent manner (Monaghan and Bell, 2005).
claims.evidence: This is stated with reference to Monaghan and Bell, 2005.

claims.claim: D44 shows promising antimalarial activity.
claims.source: While D44 shows promising antimalarial activity, it fails to alter thermostability of the FK506-binding domains of PfFKBP35 and HsFKBP12 in vitro (Atack et al., 2020), suggesting that this compound does not directly interact with PfFKBP35.
claims.evidence: This is stated with reference to Atack et al., 2020.

claims.claim: D44 fails to alter thermostability of the FK506-binding domains of PfFKBP35 and HsFKBP12 in vitro.
claims.source: While D44 shows promising antimalarial activity, it fails to alter thermostability of the FK506-binding domains of PfFKBP35 and HsFKBP12 in vitro (Atack et al., 2020), suggesting that this compound does not directly interact with PfFKBP35.
claims.evidence: This is stated with reference to Atack et al., 2020.

claims.claim: D44 does not directly interact with PfFKBP35.
claims.source: While D44 shows promising antimalarial activity, it fails to alter thermostability of the FK506-binding domains of PfFKBP35 and HsFKBP12 in vitro (Atack et al., 2020), suggesting that this compound does not directly interact with PfFKBP35.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the lack of thermostability changes in vitro.

claims.claim: PfFKBP35 has not been validated as a drug target using reverse genetics.
claims.source: Up until now, PfFKBP35 has not been validated as a drug target using reverse genetics, and the link between PfFKBP35-interacting drugs and their antimalarial activity remains elusive (Bell et al., 1994).
claims.evidence: This is stated to highlight the gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claims.claim: PfFKBP35 is essential for asexual replication of blood forms.
claims.source: Here, we generated inducible PfFKBP35 knock-out, knock-down, as well as overexpression cell lines and demonstrate that PfFKBP35 is essential for asexual replication of blood forms.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through conditional knock-out experiments.

claims.claim: The knock-out of PfFKBP35 results in reduced levels of ribosomal proteins.
claims.source: We show that the knock-out of PfFKBP35 results in reduced levels of ribosomal proteins and stalled protein synthesis.
claims.evidence: This is shown by proteomics data in G2 FKBP35KO parasites.

claims.claim: The effects of PfFKBP35 knock-out are not reflected in the parasite transcriptome.
claims.source: However, these effects are not reflected in the parasite transcriptome, indicating a vital role at the post-transcriptional level.
claims.evidence: This is shown by RNA-seq data showing minimal transcriptional changes until late G2.

claims.claim: PfFKBP35 has a vital role at the post-transcriptional level.
claims.source: However, these effects are not reflected in the parasite transcriptome, indicating a vital role at the post-transcriptional level.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the disconnect between proteomic and transcriptomic changes.

claims.claim: CETSA corroborates the high-affinity binding of FK506 to PfFKBP35.
claims.source: While the mechanistic link between PfFKBP35 and ribosome homeostasis remains elusive, our data underpins the potential of PfFKBP35 as a drug target and, using cellular thermal shift assays (CETSA), we corroborate the high-affinity binding of FK506 to PfFKBP35.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by CETSA experiments showing dose-dependent stabilization of PfFKBP35 by FK506.

claims.claim: The data does not support scenarios in which FK506 inhibits the essential function of PfFKBP35.
claims.source: Importantly, however, our data does not support scenarios in which FK506 inhibits the essential function of PfFKBP35, suggesting that it exerts its antimalarial activity in a PfFKBP35-independent manner, which has major implications for the development of future FK506-based antimalarials and/or PfFKBP35-inhibiting drugs.
claims.evidence: This is supported by dose-response experiments showing equal FK506 sensitivity in FKBP35KO and FKBP35WT parasites.

claims.claim: Despite efficient depletion of PfFKBP35 under knock-down conditions, parasites did not show apparent growth defects.
claims.source: Despite the efficient depletion of PfFKBP35 under knock-down conditions, parasites did not show apparent growth defects (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is shown by multiplication rate measurements in the NF54/iKD-FKBP35 cell line.

claims.claim: PfFKBP35 localizes to distinct foci within the parasite nucleus.
claims.source: Immunofluorescence assays (IFA) showed that PfFKBP35 localizes to distinct foci within the parasite nucleus (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence microscopy images in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: DiCre successfully deleted fkbp35 in the vast majority of parasites.
claims.source: This setup allows monitoring knock-out efficiency at the single cell level and revealed that DiCre successfully deleted fkbp35 in the vast majority of parasites (Figure 1D).
claims.evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry data in Figure 1D showing GFP expression in FKBP35KO cells.

claims.claim: FKBP35KO parasites completed intra-erythrocytic development without noticeable effects in G1.
claims.source: These FKBP35KO parasites showed a delayed death-like phenotype. In the first generation (G1), parasites completed intra-erythrocytic development without noticeable effects (Figure 1E) and entered the next generation (G2) with a multiplication rate similar to that of the FKBP35WT control population (Figure 1F).
claims.evidence: This is shown by DNA content analysis and Giemsa-stained blood smears in Figure 1E.

claims.claim: FKBP35KO parasites entered G2 with a multiplication rate similar to FKBP35WT.
claims.source: These FKBP35KO parasites showed a delayed death-like phenotype. In the first generation (G1), parasites completed intra-erythrocytic development without noticeable effects (Figure 1E) and entered the next generation (G2) with a multiplication rate similar to that of the FKBP35WT control population (Figure 1F).
claims.evidence: This is shown by multiplication rate measurements in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: In G2, FKBP35KO parasites arrested at the late trophozoite/early schizont stage (approximately 30–36 hpi).
claims.source: In G2, however, FKBP35KO parasites arrested at the late trophozoite/early schizont stage (approximately 30–36 hpi) with many cells failing to enter DNA replication in the S-phase (Figure 1E).
claims.evidence: This is shown by DNA content analysis and Giemsa-stained blood smears in Figure 1E.

claims.claim: Many FKBP35KO cells failed to enter DNA replication in the S-phase in G2.
claims.source: In G2, however, FKBP35KO parasites arrested at the late trophozoite/early schizont stage (approximately 30–36 hpi) with many cells failing to enter DNA replication in the S-phase (Figure 1E).
claims.evidence: This is shown by DNA content analysis in Figure 1E.

claims.claim: Knocking out fkbp35 at 12–18 hpi resulted in parasite death at the trophozoite/schizont stage of the subsequent generation.
claims.source: Similar to DiCre activation at 0–6 hpi, knocking out fkbp35 at 12–18 hpi resulted in parasite death at the trophozoite/schizont stage of the subsequent generation.
claims.evidence: This is stated based on experiments inducing knock-out at different time points.

claims.claim: When fkbp35 was knocked out at 24–30 hpi or 34–40 hpi in G1, parasites successfully passed through G2 before arresting in G3.
claims.source: However, when induced at 24–30 hpi or 34–40 hpi in G1, parasites did not only complete the current IDC but also successfully passed through G2 before they eventually arrested in G3 (Figure 1G).
claims.evidence: This is shown by the schematic in Figure 1G.

claims.claim: Low PfFKBP35 levels are sufficient to maintain the essential function of the protein.
claims.source: Considering that low PfFKBP35 levels are sufficient to maintain the essential function of the protein, as observed with the NF54/iKD-FKBP35 parasites (see Figure 1—figure supplement 1), it is conceivable that proteins expressed between 0 and 24 hpi, i.e. prior to deleting fkbp35 from the genome, allow parasites to enter G3.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the knock-down experiments and the timing of arrest in knock-out experiments.

claims.claim: The delayed death of FKBP35KO is reminiscent of a phenotype observed in apicoplast-deficient parasites.
claims.source: The delayed death of FKBP35KO is reminiscent of a phenotype observed in apicoplast-deficient parasites (Wiley et al., 2015; Kennedy et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is stated with references to Wiley et al., 2015 and Kennedy et al., 2019.

claims.claim: PfFKBP35 is not involved in apicoplast biology.
claims.source: We therefore tested if PfFKBP35 is involved in apicoplast biology, that is, the synthesis and/or export of isoprenoid precursors, but did not find evidence for an association with this organelle (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is shown by IPP complementation experiments in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: FKBP35KO and FKBP35WT cells did not show altered heat-susceptibility.
claims.source: Furthermore, given the reported interaction of PfFKBP35 with heat shock proteins (Leneghan and Bell, 2015; Kumar et al., 2005), we also tested the parasite`s response to heat stress, but could not detect altered heat-susceptibility between FKBP35KO and FKBP35WT cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is shown by heat shock susceptibility testing in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: FKBP35KO schizonts of G1 showed a 19-fold reduction of FKBP35 compared to the control population.
claims.source: Consistent with the efficient deletion of fkbp35 on the genomic level, FKBP35KO schizonts of G1 showed a 19-fold (18.9 ± 5.7 s.d.) reduction of FKBP35 and GFP levels were increased by 84-fold (83.7 ± 38.5 s.d.) when compared to the control population (Figure 2A, Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This is shown by proteomics data in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: GFP levels were increased by 84-fold in FKBP35KO schizonts of G1 compared to the control population.
claims.source: Consistent with the efficient deletion of fkbp35 on the genomic level, FKBP35KO schizonts of G1 showed a 19-fold (18.9 ± 5.7 s.d.) reduction of FKBP35 and GFP levels were increased by 84-fold (83.7 ± 38.5 s.d.) when compared to the control population (Figure 2A, Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This is shown by proteomics data in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: 50 parasite proteins were significantly deregulated in FKBP35KO schizonts of G1.
claims.source: Besides PfFKBP35 and GFP, 50 parasite proteins were significantly deregulated in FKBP35KO schizonts and 34 of them were found at elevated levels compared to the FKBP35WT control conditions.
claims.evidence: This is stated based on proteomics analysis.

claims.claim: 34 proteins were found at elevated levels in FKBP35KO schizonts of G1 compared to FKBP35WT.
claims.source: Besides PfFKBP35 and GFP, 50 parasite proteins were significantly deregulated in FKBP35KO schizonts and 34 of them were found at elevated levels compared to the FKBP35WT control conditions.
claims.evidence: This is stated based on proteomics analysis.

claims.claim: Gene ontology analysis indicated enrichment of the 'pre-ribosome' term among proteins elevated in FKBP35KO schizonts of G1.
claims.source: A gene ontology analysis using PANTHER (Mi et al., 2021) indicated enrichment of the 'pre-ribosome' (fold enrichment = 30.4, p-value=1.46E-5, 4/34 proteins) and 'nucleolus' (fold enrichment = 6.77, p-value=8.85E-4, 5/34 proteins) terms among these factors.
claims.evidence: This is stated based on PANTHER gene ontology analysis.

claims.claim: Gene ontology analysis indicated enrichment of the 'nucleolus' term among proteins elevated in FKBP35KO schizonts of G1.
claims.source: A gene ontology analysis using PANTHER (Mi et al., 2021) indicated enrichment of the 'pre-ribosome' (fold enrichment = 30.4, p-value=1.46E-5, 4/34 proteins) and 'nucleolus' (fold enrichment = 6.77, p-value=8.85E-4, 5/34 proteins) terms among these factors.
claims.evidence: This is stated based on PANTHER gene ontology analysis.

claims.claim: None of the 16 factors with lower abundance in FKBP35KO schizonts of G1 were associated with ribosome-related processes.
claims.source: In contrast to factors being more abundant in knock-out parasites, none of the 16 factors with lower abundance in FKBP35KO cells were associated with ribosome-related processes (Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This is stated based on proteomics analysis.

claims.claim: The accumulation of pre-ribosome and nucleolar components hints at perturbed ribosome maturation in FKBP35KO cells in G1.
claims.source: Despite being phenotypically silent in G1, the accumulation of pre-ribosome and nucleolar components hints at perturbed ribosome maturation in these cells.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the proteomics data showing accumulation of pre-ribosome components.

claims.claim: The buildup of ribosome intermediates results from reduced anabolic activity, that is, the stalling of nucleolar pre-ribosome assembly.
claims.source: Specifically, it is conceivable that the observed buildup of ribosome intermediates results from reduced anabolic activity, that is, the stalling of nucleolar pre-ribosome assembly (Nissan et al., 2002).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the proteomics data and cited literature on ribosome assembly.

claims.claim: FKBP35KO and FKBP35WT parasites were equally sensitive to the translation inhibitor cycloheximide in G1.
claims.source: Notwithstanding these effects, FKBP35KO cells were equally sensitive to the translation inhibitor cycloheximide compared to their FKBP35WT counterparts (Figure 2B), indicating that ribosome function is not compromised at this point in time (Plouffe et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This is shown by dose-response experiments in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Ribosome function is not compromised in FKBP35KO parasites in G1.
claims.source: Notwithstanding these effects, FKBP35KO cells were equally sensitive to the translation inhibitor cycloheximide compared to their FKBP35WT counterparts (Figure 2B), indicating that ribosome function is not compromised at this point in time (Plouffe et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the equal sensitivity to cycloheximide.

claims.claim: The prominent depletion of PfFKBP35 does not have a major impact on parasite viability in G1.
claims.source: This is consistent with normal cell cycle progression in G1 and unaltered multiplication rates of FKBP35KO parasites, as described above (see Figure 1E and F), and shows that the prominent depletion of PfFKBP35 does not have a major impact on parasite viability in G1.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the normal cell cycle progression and multiplication rates in G1.

claims.claim: 216 proteins were significantly deregulated in FKBP35KO trophozoites in G2 (24–30 hpi).
claims.source: In the following generation (G2, 24–30 hpi), the proteome of FKBP35KO trophozoites showed substantial differences. Despite the absence of morphological changes at this point in time, 216 proteins were significantly deregulated (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This is shown by proteomics data in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: 50 proteins were found at higher abundance in FKBP35KO trophozoites in G2 compared to FKBP35WT.
claims.source: Among these, 50 proteins were found at higher abundance compared to FKBP35WT and their gene ontology terms point toward an effect on processes involved in energy metabolism (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: This is shown by proteomics data and GO enrichment analysis in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: Gene ontology terms of proteins at higher abundance in FKBP35KO trophozoites in G2 point toward an effect on energy metabolism.
claims.source: Among these, 50 proteins were found at higher abundance compared to FKBP35WT and their gene ontology terms point toward an effect on processes involved in energy metabolism (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: This is shown by GO enrichment analysis in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: 166 of 216 deregulated factors in G2 were less abundant in FKBP35KO compared to FKBP35WT.
claims.source: The majority of deregulated factors (166 of 216) in G2, however, were less abundant in FKBP35KO compared to the FKBP35WT control cells.
claims.evidence: This is stated based on proteomics analysis.

claims.claim: 20 of the top 50 hit molecules in G2 are ribosomal proteins.
claims.source: Very prominently, 20 of the top 50 hit molecules are ribosomal proteins that, on average, show a twofold reduction (2.0 ± 0.4 s.d.) in FKBP35KO parasites (Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This is stated based on proteomics analysis.

claims.claim: Ribosomal proteins show a twofold reduction on average in FKBP35KO parasites in G2.
claims.source: Very prominently, 20 of the top 50 hit molecules are ribosomal proteins that, on average, show a twofold reduction (2.0 ± 0.4 s.d.) in FKBP35KO parasites (Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This is stated based on proteomics analysis.

claims.claim: PANTHER identified the knock-out of PfFKBP35 to mainly affect ribosome-related processes.
claims.source: It is therefore not surprising that PANTHER identified the knock-out of PfFKBP35 to mainly affect ribosome-related processes, such as 'cytoplasmic translation,' 'ribosome assembly,' and 'ribosomal large subunit biogenesis' (Figure 2D; Mi et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is shown by GO enrichment analysis in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: FKBP35KO trophozoites in G2 (24–30 hpi) showed reduced translation rates compared to the FKBP35WT control population.
claims.source: As expected, we found that FKBP35KO trophozoites in G2 (24–30 hpi) showed reduced translation rates compared to the FKBP35WT control population (Figure 2E), while protein synthesis was not affected under control conditions (rapamycin-induced DiCre activation in the NF54/DiCre parental line (Figure 2—figure supplement 1)).
claims.evidence: This is shown by SUnSET assays in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: Protein synthesis was not affected under control conditions (rapamycin-induced DiCre activation in the NF54/DiCre parental line).
claims.source: As expected, we found that FKBP35KO trophozoites in G2 (24–30 hpi) showed reduced translation rates compared to the FKBP35WT control population (Figure 2E), while protein synthesis was not affected under control conditions (rapamycin-induced DiCre activation in the NF54/DiCre parental line (Figure 2—figure supplement 1)).
claims.evidence: This is shown by SUnSET assays in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Under knock-out conditions, PfFKBP35 levels become limiting for ribosome maturation late during schizogony of G1.
claims.source: Taken together, these results indicate that, under knock-out conditions, PfFKBP35 levels become limiting for ribosome maturation late during schizogony of G1, without having immediate effects on the steady-state levels of mature ribosomes.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the proteomics and SUnSET data.

claims.claim: The knock-out of PfFKBP35 is phenotypically silent in G1.
claims.source: The knock-out of PfFKBP35 is thus phenotypically silent in G1.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the normal cell cycle progression and multiplication rates in G1.

claims.claim: In the absence of a continuous supply of mature ribosomes under FKBP35KO conditions, FKBP35KO parasites fail at maintaining translation at a level that would support normal parasite development in G2.
claims.source: In the absence of a continuous supply of mature ribosomes under FKBP35KO conditions, however, FKBP35KO parasites fail at maintaining translation at a level that would support normal parasite development in the next generation (G2).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the reduced translation rates and parasite arrest in G2.

claims.claim: The transcriptome of FKBP35KO showed a prominent reduction of steady-state fkbp35 transcripts already in TP1 (11.3-fold) compared to the FKBP35WT control population.
claims.source: As expected, the transcriptome of FKBP35KO showed a prominent reduction of steady-state fkbp35 transcripts already in TP1 (11.3-fold ± 2.0 s.d.) compared to the FKBP35WT control population (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 2).
claims.evidence: This is shown by RNA-seq data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: During peak transcription at 30–36 hpi (TP2), the difference in fkbp35 transcripts increased to 240-fold.
claims.source: During peak transcription at 30–36 hpi (TP2), this difference increased to 240-fold (238.4 ± 20.0 s.d.) and, consistent with the efficient recombination at the fkbp35 locus, these cells started transcribing gfp.
claims.evidence: This is stated based on RNA-seq data.

claims.claim: FKBP35KO cells started transcribing gfp at TP2, consistent with efficient recombination at the fkbp35 locus.
claims.source: During peak transcription at 30–36 hpi (TP2), this difference increased to 240-fold (238.4 ± 20.0 s.d.) and, consistent with the efficient recombination at the fkbp35 locus, these cells started transcribing gfp.
claims.evidence: This is stated based on RNA-seq data.

claims.claim: The transcriptome of FKBP35KO is only marginally affected up to and including 24–30 hpi in G2 (TP6).
claims.source: Notwithstanding the prominent depletion of fkbp35 transcripts, the transcriptome of FKBP35KO is only marginally affected up to and including 24–30 hpi in G2 (TP6).
claims.evidence: This is stated based on RNA-seq data.

claims.claim: At 30–36 hpi (TP7) the transcription of knock-out parasites shows major changes.
claims.source: By contrast, at 30–36 hpi (TP7) the transcription of knock-out parasites shows major changes (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This is shown by RNA-seq data in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Effects on the transcriptome at TP7 are unlikely to represent specific activities of PfFKBP35 in gene regulation.
claims.source: Considering the appearance of morphological changes in FKBP35KO at this time point, effects on the transcriptome are unlikely to represent specific activities of PfFKBP35 in gene regulation.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the timing of transcriptional changes coinciding with morphological changes.

claims.claim: Mapping the transcriptome to a high-resolution reference revealed a significant slowdown of FKBP35KO compared to FKBP35WT parasites at TP7.
claims.source: Indeed, mapping the transcriptome of individual time points to a high-resolution reference (Bozdech et al., 2003) revealed a significant slowdown of FKBP35KO compared to FKBP35WT parasites at TP7 (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is shown by transcriptome mapping in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: The slowdown indicates aborted cell cycle progression in FKBP35KO parasites during a phase characterized by a rapid increase in biomass.
claims.source: This indicates aborted cell cycle progression in FKBP35KO parasites during a phase that is characterized by a rapid increase in biomass – possibly due to a translation and/or size-dependent cell cycle checkpoint (Barnum and O'Connell, 2014).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the transcriptome mapping data and cited literature on cell cycle checkpoints.

claims.claim: At earlier time points (TP1–TP6), the transcriptomes of FKBP35KO and FKBP35WT are highly comparable.
claims.source: At earlier time points (TP1–TP6), the transcriptomes of FKBP35KO and FKBP35WT are highly comparable and the differences observed on the level of individual genes clearly fail at explaining the proteomic changes observed in FKBP35KO parasites at 24–30 hpi in G2 (TP6), reiterating that the essential activity of PfFKBP35 is linked to transcription-independent processes.
claims.evidence: This is stated based on RNA-seq data.

claims.claim: The essential activity of PfFKBP35 is linked to transcription-independent processes.
claims.source: At earlier time points (TP1–TP6), the transcriptomes of FKBP35KO and FKBP35WT are highly comparable and the differences observed on the level of individual genes clearly fail at explaining the proteomic changes observed in FKBP35KO parasites at 24–30 hpi in G2 (TP6), reiterating that the essential activity of PfFKBP35 is linked to transcription-independent processes.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the disconnect between transcriptomic and proteomic changes.

claims.claim: FK506 kills asexual blood stage parasites with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of 1.9 µM.
claims.source: Several studies conclusively demonstrated that FK506 – the most well-known ligand of mammalian FKBPs (Van Duyne et al., 1991) – binds to PfFKBP35 (Yoon et al., 2007; Bianchin et al., 2015; Kotaka et al., 2008) and kills asexual blood stage parasites with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) in the low micromolar range at 1.9 µM (Bell et al., 1994).
claims.evidence: This is stated with reference to Bell et al., 1994.

claims.claim: Live cell CETSA shows that FK506 alters the thermal stability of PfFKBP35 at very low drug concentrations when challenged at 60°C with an EC50 of 286.7 nM.
claims.source: As expected, and confirming the results above, live cell CETSA shows that FK506 alters the thermal stability of PfFKBP35 already at very low drug concentrations when challenged at 60°C with an EC50 of 286.7 nM (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This is shown by live cell CETSA data in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: More than 50 ribosomal proteins are stabilized in the presence of FK506 when challenged at 55°C in live cell CETSA.
claims.source: Interestingly, and in contrast to the protein lysate-based approach, live cell CETSA revealed that more than 50 ribosomal proteins are stabilized in the presence of FK506 when challenged at 55°C, with a median EC50 of 45.9 nM (25th percentile = 34.2, 75th percentile = 58.9).
claims.evidence: This is stated based on live cell CETSA data.

claims.claim: Ribosomal proteins were stabilized at virtually identical FK506 concentrations in live cell CETSA.
claims.source: Of note, these ribosomal proteins were stabilized at virtually identical FK506 concentrations (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 2), indicating that the drug – directly or indirectly – interacts with ribosomal complexes.
claims.evidence: This is shown by live cell CETSA data in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: FK506 directly or indirectly interacts with ribosomal complexes.
claims.source: Of note, these ribosomal proteins were stabilized at virtually identical FK506 concentrations (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 2), indicating that the drug – directly or indirectly – interacts with ribosomal complexes.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the coordinated stabilization of ribosomal proteins in live cell CETSA.

claims.claim: A drug dose-dependent increase in soluble protein abundance of ribosomal proteins was observed also under non-denaturing conditions (37°C) with a median EC50 of 1.94 µM.
claims.source: Worth mentioning, we observed a drug dose-dependent increase in soluble protein abundance of ribosomal proteins also under non-denaturing conditions, that is, at 37°C, with a median EC50 of 1.94 µM (25th percentile = 1.85, 75th percentile = 2.1) (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is shown by live cell CETSA data in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: FK506 negatively affects stability of ribosomal structures in live cells.
claims.source: The fact that FK506 solubilizes a high number of ribosomal proteins within a very narrow concentration window also at 37°C implies that these factors are liberated from the same ribosomal complex or from complexes that interact with each other and shows that FK506 negatively affects stability of ribosomal structures in live cells.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the coordinated solubilization of ribosomal proteins at 37°C in live cell CETSA.

claims.claim: The vast majority of ribosomal proteins identified in live cell CETSA are shared with those de-regulated in PfFKBP35 knock-out cells.
claims.source: Importantly, the vast majority of ribosomal proteins identified in live cell CETSA are shared with those de-regulated in PfFKBP35 knock-out cells (Figure 4E), pointing toward a shared localization of FK506 and its PfFKBP35 target in live parasites.
claims.evidence: This is shown by the Venn diagram in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: FK506 is recruited to the activity site of PfFKBP35 – most probably the nucleolar maturation sites of ribosomes.
claims.source: Together with the above-described importance of PfFKBP35 in ribosome homeostasis, these results strongly suggest that FK506 is recruited to the activity site of PfFKBP35 – most probably the nucleolar maturation sites of ribosomes – where it interacts with ribosomal complexes.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the CETSA data and the role of PfFKBP35 in ribosome homeostasis.

claims.claim: FK506 killed FKBP35WT cells with an IC50 of 1942 nM when administered at 4–10 hpi in G1.
claims.source: Consistent with published data, FK506 killed FKBP35WT cells with an IC50 of 1942 nM (+/-193 nM s.d.) when administered at 4–10 hpi in G1 (Figure 4F).
claims.evidence: This is shown by dose-response experiments in Figure 4F.

claims.claim: FKBP35KO and FKBP35WT parasites were equally sensitive to FK506.
claims.source: Surprisingly however, and despite the prominent depletion of the protein under knock-out conditions, FKBP35KO and FKBP35WT parasites were equally sensitive to FK506 (IC50 = 1741 nM ± 187 s.d.; Figure 4F; Bell et al., 1994).
claims.evidence: This is shown by dose-response experiments in Figure 4F.

claims.claim: Neither the efficient knock-down of PfFKBP35 in NF54/iKD-FKBP35 parasites nor its overexpression in NF54/iOE-FKBP35 cells resulted in the expected sensitivity change to FK506 treatment.
claims.source: Similarly, neither the efficient knock-down of PfFKBP35 in NF54/iKD-FKBP35 parasites (compare Figure 1—figure supplement 1) nor its overexpression (OE) in NF54/iOE-FKBP35 cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 3) resulted in the expected sensitivity change to FK506 treatment (Figure 4G).
claims.evidence: This is shown by dose-response experiments in Figure 4G.

claims.claim: FK506 unfolds its antimalarial activity within the same cycle after treatment.
claims.source: In addition to this apparent independence of the drug to varying PfFKBP35 levels, and in agreement with earlier studies (Bell et al., 1994; Harikishore et al., 2013b; Paul et al., 2015), FK506 unfolds its antimalarial activity within the same cycle after treatment.
claims.evidence: This is stated with references to Bell et al., 1994; Harikishore et al., 2013b; and Paul et al., 2015.

claims.claim: The immediate activity of FK506 stands in stark contrast to the delayed death-like phenotype of FKBP35KO parasites.
claims.source: This immediate activity of the drug stands in stark contrast to the delayed death-like phenotype of FKBP35KO parasites (compare Figure 1E–G), substantiating the notion that FK506 must target essential parasite factors other than PfFKBP35.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of FK506 activity kinetics and FKBP35KO phenotype.

claims.claim: FK506 must target essential parasite factors other than PfFKBP35.

claims.claim: Administering FK506 at 30–36 hpi and 36–42 hpi did not affect parasite survival in a PfFKBP35-dependent manner.
claims.source: To rule out that the timing of drug exposure is masking expected links between FK506 and PfFKBP35, we tested whether administering FK506 at 30–36 hpi and 36–42 hpi (instead of 4–10 hpi) affects parasite survival in a PfFKBP35-dependent manner (Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 4). However, we did not observe a change in FK506 susceptibility compared to FKBP35WT parasites, ruling out the possibility that FKBP35KO parasites were killed by FK506 before PfFKBP35 levels were different in the two populations.
claims.evidence: This is shown by dose-response experiments in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claims.claim: Inducing the knock-out of PfFKBP35 at 34–40 hpi and exposing parasites to FK506 in G2 did not result in differential FK506 sensitivity between FKBP35WT and FKBP35KO parasites.
claims.source: Further, to account for a scenario in which the activity of FK506 on PfFKBP35 is masked by a temporal delay between drug exposure and parasite killing, we induced the knock-out of PfFKBP35 at 34–40 hpi (instead of 0–6 hpi) and allowed FKBP35KO parasites to proceed to G2, before exposing them to different FK506 concentrations. Despite these efforts, FKBP35WT and FKBP35KO parasites were equally sensitive to FK506 (Figure 4—figure supplement 4) and the calcineurin inhibitor cyclosporin A (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
claims.evidence: This is shown by dose-response experiments in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claims.claim: FKBP35WT and FKBP35KO parasites were equally sensitive to the calcineurin inhibitor cyclosporin A.
claims.source: Despite these efforts, FKBP35WT and FKBP35KO parasites were equally sensitive to FK506 (Figure 4—figure supplement 4) and the calcineurin inhibitor cyclosporin A (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
claims.evidence: This is shown by dose-response experiments in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claims.claim: The authors failed to reproduce the previously reported dose–response effect of D44.
claims.source: In addition to FK506, we evaluated the PfFKBP35-specific inhibitor D44 (N-(2-ethylphenyl)–2-(3h-imidazo[4,5-B]pyridin-2-ylsulfanyl)acetamide) but, surprisingly, we failed to reproduce the previously reported dose–response effect (Harikishore et al., 2013b).
claims.evidence: This is stated based on dose-response experiments with D44.

claims.claim: The authors could not detect any activity of D44 on asexual replication of blood stage parasites.
claims.source: We tested D44 from two suppliers using NF54/iKO-FKBP35, NF54 wild-type and K1 parasite strains using different assay setups, including the gold standard method that is based on the incorporation of tritium-labeled hypoxanthine into DNA of replicating cells (Desjardins et al., 1979). Still, we could not detect any activity of D44 on asexual replication of blood stage parasites (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
claims.evidence: This is shown by dose-response experiments in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claims.claim: The results are in clear conflict with the perception that FK506 and D44 kill parasites by targeting PfFKBP35 exclusively.
claims.source: Taken together, these results are in clear conflict with the perception that FK506 and D44 kill parasites by targeting PfFKBP35 exclusively.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the equal FK506 sensitivity in FKBP35KO and FKBP35WT parasites and the lack of D44 activity.

claims.claim: In contrast to most other eukaryotes, the human malaria parasite P. falciparum encodes a single FKBP only.
claims.source: In contrast to most other eukaryotes, the human malaria parasite P. falciparum encodes a single FKBP only (Kumar et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: This is stated with reference to Kumar et al., 2005.

claims.claim: FK506 inhibits enzymatic activity of the PPIase domain of PfFKBP35.
claims.source: Besides demonstrating the drug's affinity to PfFKBP35 by co-crystallization, these efforts uncovered that FK506 inhibits enzymatic activity of the protein's PPIase domain (Monaghan and Bell, 2005).
claims.evidence: This is stated with reference to Monaghan and Bell, 2005.

claims.claim: PfFKBP35 is essential for intra-erythrocytic development of asexually replicating P. falciparum parasites.
claims.source: Here, we set out to investigate the role of PfFKBP35 in parasite biology. Using an inducible knock-out approach, we show that PfFKBP35 is indeed essential for intra-erythrocytic development of asexually replicating P. falciparum parasites and CETSA experiments confirmed high-affinity binding of FK506 to its PfFKBP35 target.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through conditional knock-out experiments.

claims.claim: CETSA experiments confirmed high-affinity binding of FK506 to its PfFKBP35 target.
claims.source: Here, we set out to investigate the role of PfFKBP35 in parasite biology. Using an inducible knock-out approach, we show that PfFKBP35 is indeed essential for intra-erythrocytic development of asexually replicating P. falciparum parasites and CETSA experiments confirmed high-affinity binding of FK506 to its PfFKBP35 target.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by CETSA experiments showing dose-dependent stabilization of PfFKBP35 by FK506.

claims.claim: FKBP35KO cells show reduced levels of ribosomal proteins and impaired protein synthesis on the global scale.
claims.source: While the knock-out of PfFKBP35 does not markedly affect transcription, FKBP35KO cells show reduced levels of ribosomal proteins and impaired protein synthesis on the global scale.
claims.evidence: This is shown by proteomics and SUnSET data.

claims.claim: The effects of FKBP35KO only manifest in the cycle following knock-out induction without affecting cell cycle progression in G1 or multiplication rates from G1 to G2.
claims.source: Surprisingly however, these effects, as well as the consequent death during the late trophozoite/early schizont stage, only manifest in the cycle following knock-out induction without affecting cell cycle progression in the first generation (G1) or multiplication rates from G1 to G2.
claims.evidence: This is shown by DNA content analysis and multiplication rate measurements.

claims.claim: FK506 unfolds its parasiticidal activity without a lag phase, that is, within the IDC of treatment.
claims.source: In contrast to the delayed death-like phenotype of FKBP35KO cells, FK506 unfolds its parasiticidal activity without a lag phase, that is, within the IDC of treatment (Harikishore et al., 2013b), and the dose–response relationship between FK506 and parasite death is irresponsive to altered PfFKBP35 levels.
claims.evidence: This is stated with reference to Harikishore et al., 2013b.

claims.claim: The dose–response relationship between FK506 and parasite death is irresponsive to altered PfFKBP35 levels.
claims.source: In contrast to the delayed death-like phenotype of FKBP35KO cells, FK506 unfolds its parasiticidal activity without a lag phase, that is, within the IDC of treatment (Harikishore et al., 2013b), and the dose–response relationship between FK506 and parasite death is irresponsive to altered PfFKBP35 levels.
claims.evidence: This is shown by dose-response experiments in FKBP35KO, FKBP35WT, knock-down, and overexpression cell lines.

claims.claim: The data strongly indicate that the parasite-killing activity of FK506 is PfFKBP35-independent.
claims.source: Taken together, our data strongly indicate that the parasite-killing activity of FK506 is PfFKBP35-independent.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the equal FK506 sensitivity in FKBP35KO and FKBP35WT parasites.

claims.claim: Factors associated with the nucleolus are found at higher abundance in FKBP35KO cells in G1.
claims.source: Knocking out PfFKBP35 early during intra-erythrocytic development has only minor effects on the parasite proteome in G1. Being relatively subtle, these changes may still point toward an important function of PfFKBP35: factors associated with the nucleolus – the site of ribosome biogenesis – are found at higher abundance in knock-out cells.
claims.evidence: This is stated based on proteomics analysis.

claims.claim: In G2, FKBP35KO parasites show a dramatic decrease of factors associated with ribosome- and translation-related processes.
claims.source: In the next cycle, FKBP35KO parasites show a dramatic decrease of factors associated with ribosome- and translation-related processes and, likely a consequence thereof, globally reduced protein synthesis during trophozoite development (G2, 24–30 hpi).
claims.evidence: This is stated based on proteomics analysis.

claims.claim: FKBP35KO cells show globally reduced protein synthesis during trophozoite development (G2, 24–30 hpi).
claims.source: In the next cycle, FKBP35KO parasites show a dramatic decrease of factors associated with ribosome- and translation-related processes and, likely a consequence thereof, globally reduced protein synthesis during trophozoite development (G2, 24–30 hpi).
claims.evidence: This is shown by SUnSET assays.

claims.claim: At 24–30 hpi in G2, FKBP35KO cells still show ordinary morphology.
claims.source: Importantly, at this point in time, FKBP35KO cells still show ordinary morphology and their transcriptional activity remains largely unaffected.
claims.evidence: This is stated based on microscopy and RNA-seq data.

claims.claim: The transcriptional activity of FKBP35KO cells remains largely unaffected at 24–30 hpi in G2.
claims.source: Importantly, at this point in time, FKBP35KO cells still show ordinary morphology and their transcriptional activity remains largely unaffected.
claims.evidence: This is shown by RNA-seq data.

claims.claim: The observed changes in the abundance of ribosomal factors must result from transcription-independent activity of PfFKBP35.
claims.source: The observed changes in the abundance of ribosomal factors must therefore result from transcription-independent activity of PfFKBP35.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the disconnect between proteomic and transcriptomic changes.

claims.claim: Low PfFKBP35 levels inhibit ribosome maturation in G1, explaining the accumulation of (pre-) ribosomal factors.
claims.source: While ribosomal components are present at higher levels in G1, they are drastically reduced in FKBP35KO cells in G2. These opposing effects likely result from PfFKBP35 activity in a shared cellular process. Specifically, it is conceivable that low PfFKBP35 levels inhibit ribosome maturation in G1, explaining the accumulation of (pre-) ribosomal factors.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the proteomics data showing accumulation of pre-ribosome components in G1.

claims.claim: While the levels of functional ribosomes are sufficient to support continued translation in G1, ribosomes likely become limiting in G2.
claims.source: While the levels of functional ribosomes are sufficient to support continued translation in G1, ribosomes likely become limiting in the next generation (G2), which eventually results in stalled translation activity and concomitant parasite death at the onset of schizogony.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the normal translation in G1 and reduced translation in G2.

claims.claim: Limiting ribosomes in G2 eventually result in stalled translation activity and concomitant parasite death at the onset of schizogony.
claims.source: While the levels of functional ribosomes are sufficient to support continued translation in G1, ribosomes likely become limiting in the next generation (G2), which eventually results in stalled translation activity and concomitant parasite death at the onset of schizogony.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the reduced translation and parasite arrest in G2.

claims.claim: Transcription of FKBP35KO cells becomes apparent only during late trophozoite/early schizont development in G2 (30–36 hpi).
claims.source: In contrast to the significant effects on the protein levels in G2, transcription of FKBP35KO cells remains largely unaffected by the loss of PfFKBP35 and becomes apparent only during late trophozoite/early schizont development in G2 (30–36 hpi); that is, at a time during which cell cycle progression is slowed down in FKBP35KO parasites.
claims.evidence: This is shown by RNA-seq data.

claims.claim: At 30–36 hpi in G2, the transcriptional signature of FKBP35KO parasites is dominated by the slowed progression through intra-erythrocytic development.
claims.source: In fact, at this stage the transcriptional signature of FKBP35KO parasites is dominated by the slowed progression through intra-erythrocytic development, rather than resulting from specific gene regulatory events.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the transcriptome mapping data.

claims.claim: The stalling of cell cycle progression is consistent with the observed effects on ribosome homeostasis and protein synthesis.
claims.source: While this stalling is consistent with the observed effects on ribosome homeostasis and protein synthesis, it demonstrates that, in contrast to certain FKBP family members in other organisms (Ghartey-Kwansah et al., 2018), PfFKBP35 does not have apparent roles in transcriptional control.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the timing of transcriptional changes and the effects on ribosomes and translation.

claims.claim: PfFKBP35 does not have apparent roles in transcriptional control.

claims.evidence: This is inferred from the lack of specific transcriptional changes in FKBP35KO parasites.

claims.claim: CETSA performed on protein lysates identified a number of parasite factors binding to FK506.
claims.source: Since binding of FK506 to PfFKBP35 alone cannot explain the drug's antimalarial activity, we aimed to identify additional FK506 targets. CETSA performed on protein lysates identified a number of parasite factors binding to FK506.
claims.evidence: This is shown by lysate-based CETSA data.

claims.claim: The adenosine-methyltransferase MT-A70 (PF3D7_0729500) was stabilized by FK506 with an EC50 of 2.0 µM.
claims.source: The adenosine-methyltransferase MT-A70 (PF3D7_0729500) and the pre-mRNA-splicing factor CEF1 (PF3D7_1033600), for instance, were stabilized by FK506 with EC50 concentrations of 2.0 and 3.1 µM, respectively.
claims.evidence: This is stated based on lysate-based CETSA data.

claims.claim: The pre-mRNA-splicing factor CEF1 (PF3D7_1033600) was stabilized by FK506 with an EC50 of 3.1 µM.
claims.source: The adenosine-methyltransferase MT-A70 (PF3D7_0729500) and the pre-mRNA-splicing factor CEF1 (PF3D7_1033600), for instance, were stabilized by FK506 with EC50 concentrations of 2.0 and 3.1 µM, respectively.
claims.evidence: This is stated based on lysate-based CETSA data.

claims.claim: Numerous attempts to prove that FK506 indeed inhibits essential PfFKBP35 functions failed.
claims.source: However, numerous attempts to prove that FK506 indeed inhibits essential PfFKBP35 functions failed: neither knocking out PfFKBP35 at different time points nor adding FK506 to different stages of FKBP35KO parasites could provide evidence for a PfFKBP35-dependent effect.
claims.evidence: This is stated based on multiple experimental approaches.

claims.claim: Either the binding of FK506 does not interfere with the essential role of PfFKBP35, or PfFKBP35 is inhibited only at high FK506 concentrations that also inhibit other essential factors.

claims.evidence: This is inferred from the failure to demonstrate PfFKBP35-dependent effects of FK506.

claims.source: In this context, it is worth mentioning that parasites remain unaffected by a highly efficient knock-down of endogenous PfFKBP35 (observed with NF54/iKD-FKBP35; compare Figure 1—figure supplement 1), which demonstrates that very low protein levels are sufficient to maintain the essential function of PfFKBP35.

claims.source: It is thus conceivable that high FK506 concentrations are required to fully inhibit PfFKBP35 – a view that is further supported by data obtained with the live cell CETSA approach discussed hereafter.

claims.source: These results indicate that the FK506/PfFKBP35 pair interacts with ribosomal complexes and that FK506 is able to induce the dissociation of these ribosomal structures under physiological conditions.

claims.claim: FK506 is able to induce the dissociation of ribosomal structures under physiological conditions.
